scenes.tts: The brain and spinal cord begin as a flat sheet of cells. By about the fourth week, how do they become a sealed tube?
scenes.visual: Title card: Narrow First, Then Fold. A top view of an embryo's back with a flat sheet highlighted along the midline; a clock reads: end of about week 4 after fertilization.
scenes.narration: The brain and spinal cord begin as a flat sheet of cells. By about the fourth week, how do they become a sealed tube?

scenes.tts: This sheet is the neural plate, along the midline of the embryo's back. On either side, surface ectoderm will form the skin.
scenes.visual: Top view: the outer layer labelled ectoderm; a midline band glows, labelled neural plate; surface ectoderm (future skin) on both sides. A slicing plane passes across the back and the cross-section drops out beside it, dorsal side up, with the notochord beneath the midline.
scenes.narration: This sheet is the neural plate, along the midline of the embryo's back. On either side, surface ectoderm will form the skin.

scenes.tts: Step one, shaping. The cells grow taller, and the plate narrows from side to side and lengthens from head to tail.
scenes.visual: Step 1, Shaping. Cross-section thickens; top view narrows across and lengthens head to tail. Animation pauses on the step label.
scenes.narration: Step one, shaping. The cells grow taller, and the plate narrows from side to side and lengthens from head to tail.

scenes.tts: Hold on to this step. If the plate's middle stays wide, the folds may have too far to go.
scenes.visual: The step 1 label stays highlighted with a pin icon.
scenes.narration: Hold on to this step. If the plate's middle stays wide, the folds may have too far to go.

scenes.tts: Step two, bending. The plate creases at hinge points, and its edges rise as the neural folds.
scenes.visual: Step 2, Bending. Cross-section creases at a midline hinge over the notochord; the edges rise, labelled neural folds.
scenes.narration: Step two, bending. The plate creases at hinge points, and its edges rise as the neural folds.

scenes.tts: Step three. The folds move toward the midline, meet, and fuse.
scenes.visual: Step 3, Meeting and fusion. The fold tips meet at the top and fuse.
scenes.narration: Step three. The folds move toward the midline, meet, and fuse.

scenes.tts: Step four. The tube separates from the skin, which seals over it.
scenes.visual: Step 4, Separation. The closed tube detaches; the epidermis seals over it.
scenes.narration: Step four. The tube separates from the skin, which seals over it.

scenes.tts: Now look from above. In the mouse, closure begins at several sites and spreads from each like a zipper.
scenes.visual: Mouse-style top view of the folds; zipping begins at separate sites and spreads outward. Label: mouse.
scenes.narration: Now look from above. In the mouse, closure begins at several sites and spreads from each like a zipper.

scenes.tts: The first site is called Closure one. It sits at the boundary between the hindbrain and the spinal cord.
scenes.caption: The first site is called Closure 1. It sits at the boundary between the hindbrain and the spinal cord.
scenes.visual: The first site flashes, labelled Closure 1, at the hindbrain and spinal cord boundary.
scenes.narration: The first site is called Closure 1. It sits at the boundary between the hindbrain and the spinal cord.

scenes.tts: A stretch that does not close stays open for the rest of pregnancy. Where it stays open names the defect.
scenes.visual: A flat map of the tube from head end to lower end, sealed throughout. Label: schematic.
scenes.narration: A stretch that does not close stays open for the rest of pregnancy. Where it stays open names the defect.

scenes.tts: If the head end fails, the result is anencephaly. The exposed brain tissue degenerates.
scenes.visual: The map opens at the head end, labelled anencephaly.
scenes.narration: If the head end fails, the result is anencephaly. The exposed brain tissue degenerates.

scenes.tts: If the lower end fails, the cord itself lies in an open lesion. This is my-uh-low-muh-ning-go-seal, the open form of spina bifida.
scenes.caption: If the lower end fails, the cord itself lies in an open lesion. This is myelomeningocele, the open form of spina bifida.
scenes.visual: The map opens at the lower end, labelled myelomeningocele (open spina bifida).
scenes.narration: If the lower end fails, the cord itself lies in an open lesion. This is myelomeningocele, the open form of spina bifida.

scenes.tts: In the mouse, if Closure one never happens, the tube stays open from the midbrain down the spine. This is cray-nee-oh-ray-kiss-kih-sis.
scenes.caption: In the mouse, if Closure 1 never happens, the tube stays open from the midbrain down the spine. This is craniorachischisis.
scenes.visual: The map opens from the midbrain to the lower end, labelled craniorachischisis; the Closure 1 site is marked with a cross.
scenes.narration: In the mouse, if Closure 1 never happens, the tube stays open from the midbrain down the spine. This is craniorachischisis.

scenes.tts: So why would a tube fail? One reason: the folds can close only a gap their bending can cover.
scenes.visual: The cross-section returns with two folds raised either side of the midline. Card: One reason a tube can fail. The folds can close only a gap their bending can cover.
scenes.narration: So why would a tube fail? One reason: the folds can close only a gap their bending can cover.

scenes.tts: And the midline between them sets that gap. Narrowing it comes early and overlaps folding. Failures of bending, fusion or sealing are other routes.
scenes.visual: The midline strip between the folds is highlighted; a double arrow across it labelled: the gap. Small note: bending, fusion or sealing can also fail.
scenes.narration: And the midline between them sets that gap. Narrowing it comes early and overlaps folding. Failures of bending, fusion or sealing are other routes.

scenes.tts: Takeaway: narrowing starts first and keeps going as the folds rise. Where closure fails names the defect.
scenes.visual: Closing card: narrowing starts first and overlaps folding; where closure fails names the defect; narrow first, then fold.
scenes.narration: Takeaway: narrowing starts first and keeps going as the folds rise. Where closure fails names the defect.
